evidence.field: 考; formation analyses and examples, lines 171–179
evidence.text: The dictionary presents a 老-based account: early Western Zhou bronze writing used 老 for both ‘old’ and ‘father’; adding 丂 as a phonetic marker distinguished 考, and the 考 form commonly omits the lower 匕 of 老. It also reports a competing account in which 丂 was an original graph, borrowed for ‘father’, and 老 was added as a semantic classifier; the dictionary says early bronze use of 丂 for ‘father’ gives this account some support, but considers the 老-based account a better explanation of early Western Zhou evidence. It reports bronze 考 for ‘father’ in 兮仲鐘 and for ‘consider/estimate’ in 中山王鼎, alongside separate phonetic uses for 孝 and 巧 in named bronze and Warring States texts. The entry supplies no dates for those particular examples and does not establish a semantic bridge from ‘father’ to ‘examine/test’.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考

evidence.field: 丂; graph interpretation and attested uses, lines 108–112
evidence.text: The entry attributes to 屈萬里 an interpretation of oracle-bone and bronze 丂 as a branch form, proposed as an early pictographic form of 柯; it says he earlier followed 說文 in interpreting it as an axe handle. The same page describes 丂 as a cane in the 老-man depiction, and reports oracle-bone use as a place name, bronze use for ‘father’ and 孝, and Warring States use read as 巧. The referent and original name or pronunciation of the depicted object are not independently established here, so an object-name-based borrowing account remains uncertain.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 丂 component analysis

evidence.field: 考; pronunciation, variant forms, and cited old dictionaries, lines 17–32 and 118–126
evidence.text: The Ministry dictionary gives Mandarin kǎo, lists 丂 and 攷 among forms classed as variants of 考, quotes the traditional Shuowen analysis ‘從老省，丂聲’, and records 苦浩切 under 集韻. This establishes the dictionary’s own pronunciation and variant classification, but does not date the overlap of 考 and 攷.

gaps: The source pages do not provide dates for the cited inscription and bamboo examples, so the earliest attested date for each sense remains unresolved. The ‘consider/estimate’ example is not by itself evidence of a chronological shift to modern ‘examine/test’.

The object represented by 丂 and its original name/pronunciation remain disputed; reconstructions of the character 丂 do not independently establish the name of a depicted object or an object-name-based loan.

The local Baxter–Sagart readings differ in Old Chinese while sharing Middle Chinese khawX: 丂 *C.qʰˤuʔ versus 考 *k-r̥ˤuʔ. The official project site was inspected but the character-specific supplementary data were not externally opened in this pass. Unicode Unihan pages for both code points failed, leaving externally verified current kMandarin records unavailable.
The separate graphic and chronological relationship of 攷 (攴 plus 丂) to 考 was not investigated beyond the Ministry dictionary listing 攷 as a variant.

The Commons oracle file page opened, but direct source and rights metadata could not be confirmed from the retrieved lines; the bronze-style vector is the better documented candidate. No actual artifact photograph or Xiaoxuetang character-specific record and CC0 notice was verified.
